Two facts carry the whole bank, and for weeks neither was stated
anywhere plainly. The register listed OPEN WORK and the findings log
recorded every twist of the debugging, so the surface grew by one entry
per discovery while never once giving the position. **Reporting the
process is not reporting the position.**

| | items | what is true |

| **Choose a Response (cr-v1 — archived 2026-08-18)** | 0 | **Known broken.** Solvable without the audio, on two independent instruments. |
| Everything else | 5,413 | **Not known to be broken** — never read by a person |

0.0% is a quality problem. The rest is a scheduling
problem, and it is blocked on one 20-minute task: **B2 — the two never-read cohorts (B4 passed 2026-08-15)**.

Every cohort a human has actually read came back clean. The one that failed a human check — Choose a Response cr-v1 — was archived on 2026-08-18 and replaced by cr-v7.

### Every attempt to fix Choose a Response (cr-v1 — archived 2026-08-18)

`blind` is how often three AI solvers pick the right answer with the
audio withheld. `control` is the best a fixed-letter guesser could do.
**A gap near zero is the goal.** Nothing has reached it.

| attempt | changed | blind | control | gap | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **cr-v1 — original authoring** | The batch as first written. | 76.9% | — | *not recorded* | FAILED |
| **narrow repair** | Rewrote only the 24 options with the clearest defect, rather than rebuilding. | 74.4% | 29.2% | **+45.2** | REFUTED |
| **cr-v3** | New method: distractors written as the correct reply to a near-miss version of the spoken line. | 77.8% | 25% | **+52.8** | FAILED |
| **cr-v4** | Varied the spoken line: good news, a request, an offer, a correction, an apology, an announcement. | 47.2% | 25% | **+22.2** | INCONCLUSIVE |
| **cr-v5** | cr-v4 plus a ban on one give-away phrase the solvers named. | 72.2% | 25% | **+47.2** | FAILED |
| **cr-v6** | cr-v4's brief held EXACTLY — nothing added, nothing removed, fresh scenarios. The replication test. | 72.2% | 25% | **+47.2** | FAILED |
| **cr-v7** | New METHOD, not a new brief: four mutually exclusive worlds per item authored symmetrically (each world has its own line AND reply; 1,584 kill-quotes machine-verified), then a seeded RNG picks the spoken world AFTER the text is frozen — no author ever knows the key. | 26.4% | 25% | **+1.4** | CLEARED |

The shape of that table is the finding: **each attempt removes the
previous tell and introduces a new one.** Why each failed:

- **cr-v1 — original authoring** — The brief fixed four kinds of wrong answer — over-formal, rude, dismissive, topic-shifting. The key is then simply the option that is none of them, and all three solvers named the roster unprompted.
- **narrow repair** — Removing one of four slots leaves three, and the key is still the option that is none of them. Moved the score ~3 points; I predicted 28.4% beforehand and was wrong by 46.
- **cr-v3** — The method was sound but every spoken line was the same kind of line — two-part bad news — so the key was always rueful acceptance and the distractors always relief or disbelief. The roster moved from the answers up to the questions and got stronger.
- **cr-v4** — BEST RESULT. Solvers stayed confident, used the same heuristic, and got worse — the signature of a tell actually removed. Inside the pre-registered 20-30 band at n=12, so not a pass, and never re-tested unchanged.
- **cr-v5** — The ban stripped questions out of the wrong answers, so pre-flight flagged an imbalance, and repairing THAT by hand made every wrong answer sound hedgy — "I thought", "I gather" — in 6 of 36 distractors and 0 of 12 keys. I reintroduced a roster while fixing a cosmetic check.
- **cr-v6** — +47.2, indistinguishable from cr-v5 and from the original defect: cr-v4's +22.2 was a draw, not a method. This settled that no BRIEF fixes the task type — the authorship asymmetry (the key is the reply to the real line, the distractors are something else) survives every authoring rule.
- **cr-v7** — CLEARED AND SHIPPED 2026-08-18 on Andy's explicit approval. The key is statistically independent of every text feature by construction; the solvers' loudest heuristic was counted against the population and points nowhere (15.8% where chance is 25%). S1 −16.7, S2 +1.4, post-cohesion re-attack +5.6, all under the pre-registered +30 kill bar. 132 items live as cohort cr-v7; the 63 old rows archived; the Listening blueprint restored to the ETS shape (14 delivered).

## 1. Where every cohort actually stands — MEASURED

`blind` is 3 AI solvers with the source withheld, against a 25%
control. `human` is a real reviewer under the same protocol. **Where
the two disagree the human wins** — the finding of 2026-08-06, and on
Announcement and Daily Life the model was indeed the one that was wrong.

Two qualifications, both learned the hard way:

- `human` is the **best single reader**, never a pooled average. The
  question is whether a person *can* shortcut these items, and one
  reader who can settles it. Pooling a diligent reader with a cautious
  one produced "cleared by hand" for a cohort scoring 74.4% blind.
- The human winning does not mean the model was noise. Where a reader
  also clears the control by a wide margin, the two AGREE and the cohort
  is confirmed broken — which is what happened to Choose a Response.

### Excluded from the human column — model-assisted

34 reviews were entered through the human UI with a model
doing the answering. They are kept as data and marked `model_assisted`
(migration 079); they do NOT feed the `human` column above, because that
column is worth exactly one thing — being the number a model did not
produce.

- `craft-and-structure-2026-08-06` — 14/14 (100.0%)
- `academic-passage-2026-08-06` — 13/20 (65.0%)

**79.4% assisted vs 19.5% by hand.** That gap is
the point: a model reading four options scores far above a person doing
the same, which is exactly why one of the two instruments has to stay
human. Unfiltered, SAT Craft and Structure read *CONFIRMED BROKEN — both
instruments agree* on blind 97.4% + "human" 100%, condemning 211 items on
a model agreeing with itself.

## 4. Settled — do not redo

- **SAT Math derivational hub.** Claimed "bank-wide, 64.4%". It was 131 items of 820. All repaired; both cohorts now score BELOW chance. → `scripts/study-bank/MATH-HUB-RESULT.md`
- **The cheap elimination gate cannot replace the blind attack.** Fires on 3 of 32 items in a repaired batch. Once distractors are well-formed it stops correlating with anything. → `scripts/study-bank/CRV3-RESULT.md`
- **The option-balance check does not work.** Predicted a 2.7pt spread across three batches whose real margins spanned +14.6 to +40.4, and its inputs were not reproducible between labellers. → `scripts/study-bank/OPTION-BALANCE-RESULT.md`
- **Figures do not leak their answers.** 0 leaks across 164 graphics, with a 7-fixture self-test proving the checker fires on real ones and stays quiet on well-formed charts. → `scripts/study-bank/check-graphic-leak.mjs`
- **Reviews are bound to the content they judged.** Migration 076 applied. Scoring reads study_item_reviews_fresh, so editing a reviewed item visibly invalidates its review instead of silently keeping it. → `database/migrations/076_review_content_binding.sql`
- **The grader is not calibrated, and cannot be from public data.** Only two scored ETS samples exist for our task types. Do not tune prompts against them — two items cannot support fitting.

## 5. Found while fixing

Appended in the same commit as the work that surfaced it. A finding
recorded only in a commit message is a finding nobody reads.

- **2026-09-01** — THE PRICE SHOWN WAS NOT THE PRICE CHARGED, on two live ISEE sections. The assemble route reserves creditCostForTest(family, block.key) — the blueprint block key. The topic sheet derived its own key by title-casing the topic slug and lowercasing it back, which for two sections produced a string that is not in SECTION_CREDIT_COST at all: isee-quant-reasoning -> "quant_reasoning" against the route's "quant", and isee-math-achievement -> "math_achievement" against "mathach". Both fell through to the `?? 1` default, so the sheet displayed 1 credit while the route reserved 2. Two paths computing one number differently, each internally consistent — the same shape as the band-vs-percent bug in CLAUDE.md. Both sides now read the same block key, pinned by a test over the two source files. HOW IT WAS FOUND MATTERS MORE THAN THE BUG: a break-test came back GREEN. Removing ssat/isee from parseTestSlug failed nothing, which looked like dead code and was actually a coverage gap — that family feeds credit pricing and the path card, and neither had a test. A reversion that breaks nothing is evidence about the TESTS, not about the code. _(fixed on the spot)_
- **2026-09-01** — THE SERVE-TIME CHOICE SHUFFLE IS LOAD-BEARING AND HAD NO TEST AT ALL. Measured across the live maths bank: every cohort is middle-heavy — the key rarely sits at the smallest or largest option, because good distractor practice brackets the answer with over- and under-applied errors. sat/v2 (n=710) puts 72% of keys in the middle two ranks against 50% expected. THE EXPOSURE IS A CONJUNCTION, and my first framing was too broad: a rank skew only becomes a letter tell where options are actually PRINTED in order. SSAT/ISEE cohorts are 65-100% ascending (today's authored: 100%); sat/v2 is 8%. So sat/v2 is skewed and structurally immune, while FOUR SSAT/ISEE cohorts are both skewed and sorted — worth about +13 points to "never pick the extremes" with no question read. The reading bank has the same shape for a different reason: in reading-worlds-s5, variant W1 carries the unqualified endorsement in 7 of 9 topics. Only shuffleDrawnChoices keeps either out of the served item, and a future change preserving source order "for fidelity" (real SSAT and ISEE do print ascending) would silently reinstate a deterministic key position. Now guarded and break-tested. check-key-rank-spread.mjs measures when it could safely be retired. THE UNDERLYING SKEW IS STILL IN THE BANK — the guard protects the serving path, it does not repair the four cohorts. _(fixed on the spot)_
- **2026-09-01** — SSAT AND ISEE WERE SERVABLE BY API AND UNREACHABLE BY A STUDENT for a full day. 769 gated items, two full forms per section, a working assemble route and a correct result screen — and three separate UI blocks: TEST_THEMES had no entry so no card rendered; parseTestSlug omitted both families; and startBankTest opened with a bare `return` for anything not SAT or TOEFL, so Start did NOTHING — no spinner, no message. It survived because every check I ran exercised the API path; nothing exercised the UI path. Sections now resolve by SLUG through ADMISSION_TOPIC_SLUGS, not by the title-cased section name, because ssat-quant-1 title-cases to "Quant 1" (matching no blueprint section) and the two SSAT quantitative blocks differ only by key while sharing a bank section — a name lookup cannot tell them apart. ssat-experimental is deliberately unmapped: a topic row exists because the real SSAT has one, but it is unscored and excluded from the blueprint, so serving it would spend 15 minutes on questions that do not count. _(fixed on the spot)_
- **2026-09-01** — THE QC SWEEP PANEL COULD NEVER LOAD, and could never show why. Two bugs producing one symptom. (1) The route filtered verdicts with .in('item_id', ids) over every item; supabase-js sends a select as a GET, so 769 UUIDs became a 28,452-character URL, far past any practical cap, and the request never returned. (2) The load effect guarded on open && !data && !loading with no err, so a failure set the error, cleared loading, and immediately refetched — an infinite retry rendering as a permanent "Loading the bank…" with the error never on screen long enough to read. The verdicts table is small by construction and is now read whole and joined in memory, paged so a 1000-row cap cannot truncate it; err is in the guard and there is a Try again button. NOTE ON MY OWN TESTING: the first test for (2) was VACUOUS — counting fetches after an induced failure passed with the retry loop restored, because jsdom does not flush the effect cycle within any assertable window. Replaced with a source pin that does fail on reversion. Second vacuous test of that session. _(fixed on the spot)_
- **2026-09-01** — TWO STALE NUMBERS I HAD BEEN REPEATING, both found only by computing them. (1) The bank holds 769 SSAT/ISEE items, not 645 — stale from before that day's cohorts. (2) Live item count is 4,808, not 4,812; the higher figure counted 4 unverified TOEFL rows that will not serve. Also corrected in shipped-tests.ts: the gate said SSAT and ISEE serve "EXACTLY ONE full form each as of 2026-08-29", true when written and false two days later once A17 closed — both now serve two (SSAT reading 83 drawable/40 needed, ISEE math 174/84, SSAT verbal 124/60). Reading counts are AFTER the 3-items-per-passage cap, so the raw bank count overstates repeatability: SSAT reading holds 138 items but only 83 are drawable into one form. The comment now says to re-run verify-admission-forms.mjs rather than trust it. _(fixed on the spot)_
- **2026-09-01** — BUILD BROKEN BY MY OWN TESTS, and the reason generalises. - **2026-09-04** — THE TWO SAT MATH "HARD" BATCHES BOTH FAILED, FOR DIFFERENT REASONS, AND ONE OF THE FAILURES IS INVISIBLE TO EVERY EXISTING CHECKER. It reported 34.6% on Advanced Math while the options-only attack (stem stripped entirely, four bare values, keys dealt flat) scored **51.4% across three solvers, +26.4 over control**, and 9 of the 10 items every solver got were symbolic sets. `check-symbolic-hub.mjs` (new) tokenises each option and scores the key's one-edit degree against its siblings, with tie-splitting so the credits over four key positions sum to exactly 1.0000 — its self-test fails if they do not. Run against the WHOLE live population rather than a sample, per this file's own corollary: Advanced Math 33.1%, Algebra 35.6%, Geometry 29.0%, PSDA 27.6%, all 955 structured items **31.3% against a 25% control (+6.3)**. So the live bank carries a mild, real elevation concentrated in the two algebraic domains — nothing like the +23.9 of the new Advanced batch, and not a rewrite programme. **THE POSITIONAL CYCLE THAT DOES NOT MATTER, AND WHY IT LOOKED LIKE IT DID.** The with-source grader found Algebra's key index to be exactly `(item - 1) mod 4` on all 24 items, and Advanced's to repeat `0 3 2 1 3 0 1 2` twice — a perfect 6/6/6/6 per-cohort histogram, so the letter-spread check reads clean, which is recorded tell #2 in CLAUDE.md in its purest form. It reaches no student: `shuffleDrawnChoices` reseeds every drawn item's options per session, and every SAT draw passes through it. Recorded because the distinction is the useful part — **a positional tell is neutralised by a serve-time shuffle; a derivational hub is not, because it is a relation among the option TEXTS and survives any reordering.** That is also why the options-only attack could not see the cycle: it deals keys flat, so it destroyed the tell it was not testing for and scored Algebra 18.1%, BELOW chance. Two instruments, each blind to the other's defect. **DIFFICULTY, THE FOURTH BATCH RUNNING.** Algebra graded hard 2 / medium 20 / easy 2; Advanced hard 4 / medium 16 / easy 4 — both self-labelled all-hard. With SEC v1 (1 hard of 24) and SEC v2 (4 of 16) that is four consecutive commissioned-hard batches returning 2-25% hard, across two domains and separate authors: **Claude-authored "hard" SAT items come out medium, reliably, and the label must be taken from the grader and not the author.** `math-bank-helper.mjs` stores `raw.difficulty` from the batch and uses the grader's only to gate acceptance, so the batch file was rewritten from the qc before insert; without that, 22 medium items would have entered the hard route the exercise existed to fill. TOOLING: `sec-qc-aggregate.mjs` wrote `passage_needed: true` as a literal while the solvers report the field per item — a check that could not fail, the same shape as the submit test that stayed green after its rule was deleted. - **2026-09-04** — THE SKILLS MADE THE BATCHES WORSE, MEASURED THREE TIMES, AND THE WITH-SOURCE GRADE SAID ALL THREE WERE FINE. **SAT Information and Ideas (`sat-ii-hard-v1`) is the worst blind margin this register holds: 93.0% with the passages withheld (94.7 / 94.7 / 89.5), against a 25% control and a +36.2 family bar — a margin of +68.0, and 31 of 31 confident picks correct across the three solvers.** It had already passed a with-source key grade unanimously: three graders returned IDENTICAL pick sequences on all 24 items, 19 survived the acceptance rule, and every one of those 19 was then answerable without its passage. The two grades disagree completely and the no-source one is the real one. All three attackers named the same invariant unprompted and in their own words: **the key is always the option that narrows the claim, and the distractors are the ones that complete it** — "does not by itself indicate", "only partly", "bears on one stage", "most ... though a modest", "owes less to X than to Y". Discard every option that finishes the thought and keep the one that says this far and no further, and you have half the section at high confidence with no reading. It is recorded tell #3 (identical key PROSE) in a new dress, and none of the five structural proxies sees it, because it is a stance rather than a string. HELD, not inserted. **ACT Reading v5: 94.4% on the SIBLING-FREE attack (nine passage-disjoint files, a different solver each), 26 of 28 confident picks right** — worse than v4's 91.7% and far worse than the 76-79% of the round-1/round-2 forms the co-founder actually sat and scored 10.0% on. Solvers named three separate leaks: stems that pre-state the contrast the options resolve, vocabulary-in-context items whose quoted collocation is self-sufficient ("has no purchase in law"), and distractors generated by a small fixed set of transformations of the key, so the key is recoverable as the option that has not been transformed. **THE PATTERN ACROSS ALL OF THIS IS THE FINDING.** v4, v5 and I&I were the first cohorts authored against the new `.claude/skills/bank-*` files, which enumerate every recorded tell and forbid it. They are MORE model-guessable than the forms written before the skills existed. Forbidding a shape in a brief does not remove it; it selects the complement, and the complement is equally learnable. This is the CLAUDE.md corollary confirmed a fourth time, now with the brief being our own documentation. The one method that has ever produced a clean cohort is cr-v7's: author all four options symmetrically and let a seeded RNG pick the key AFTER text freeze, so the key is independent of every text feature BY CONSTRUCTION rather than by an author's restraint. Two of the three I&I attackers proposed exactly that unprompted ("require that at least one distractor per set be equally qualified", "let a distractor be the cautious one and the key sometimes be the flat assertion"). **DECISION: no repair brief for I&I and no further ACT Reading forms.** act-reading-v4 stays staged as the single specimen that tests whether the model number means anything post-B7; adding v5 and v6 to the staging pile answers nothing before the human sample does. v5 and v6 are authored and held on disk, unattacked for v6. **A DEAD CONSTANT WAS WRONG AND AN AUTHORING AGENT FOUND IT.** `ENGLISH_QUOTAS` in act-test.ts read Production of Writing [38,43] / Knowledge of Language [18,23] / Conventions [38,43] — making Conventions a third of the English test when it is the majority category — while the three places that DRIVE behaviour (test-specs.ts patterns_en and patterns_ko, and the generate route's 0.305 split) all carried ACT's real 29-32 / 13-19 / 51-56. Nothing read ENGLISH_QUOTAS except the ACT_QUOTAS map, which is why a wrong blueprint sat there through a commit that says "verified against ACT's 2025-26 forms". Corrected and pinned by act-english-quotas.test.ts. The break-test is the instructive part: reverting all three values fails the majority-category and exact-share assertions but PASSES the "ranges admit a form summing to 100" assertion, because 94-109 contains 100 — the plausibility check the numbers were presumably eyeballed against is exactly the check that cannot catch them. My first break-test reverted only one of the three values and reported three failures; the honest number is two. → **B6**, **A21**

- **2026-09-04** — VARYING THE KEY'S ROLE WORKED, AND UNCOVERED THE SIXTH TELL UNDERNEATH IT. `sat-cs-hard-v1` (24 Craft and Structure items) is the first batch authored with the CLAUDE.md corollary applied deliberately rather than as a prohibition: the author varied WHAT THE KEY DOES from item to item — only 2 of 8 Text Structure keys are refutation-shaped, one key is the SUPERSEDED claim, one is a reconciling reading, one is corroboration — and self-attacked from the options alone before finalising, rewriting two items that were shape-solvable. **No-source attack: 70.8 / 79.2 / 66.7, mean 72.2%, margin +47.2 against a +36.2 bar.** Still a fail. That is what a healthy set looks like." The prescription in this file is now measured, not just argued: requiring the load-bearing element to vary across items removes the tell it targets, and moves the number a long way. **What it does not do is clear the bar, because a second leak was underneath.** Two of three solvers found the same new one independently and named its mechanism: **the key is the only option built around the exact phrase the question stem quotes, while all three distractors argue adjacent positions drawn from the topic's general discourse.** One solver used that single rule to answer six of the eight cross-text items with no stance reading at all. It is an asymmetry of PROVENANCE — the key was authored FROM the stem, the distractors were authored from the subject — and it is invisible to every letter, length, punctuation, pivot and option-family check, making it the sixth entry in that list and the second (after the I&I stance tell) that no cheap proxy can see. The indicated fix is symmetrising rather than prohibiting, which is the cr-v7 direction: write at least one distractor that also grips the stem's own number or phrase and misuses it, so that specificity stops being a signature. A third, smaller leak in the same batch: on function items the key can be picked by matching the quoted sentence's verb type against each option's verb, because the distractors are written to be formally incompatible with the sentence rather than wrong about where it sits in the argument. **C&S is HELD.** Running score for the day: three SAT R&W hard batches authored, none banked; the two math batches split, Algebra in at graded difficulty and Advanced held. → **B6**

- **2026-09-04** — THE SEVENTH PROXY WORKS, COVERS 2% OF THE BANK, AND EXPLAINS NONE OF THE MARGIN. Solver C's report on `sat-cs-hard-v1` named a tell that is, unusually, a STRING rather than a stance: the key is the option carrying a grant-verb frame ("By **granting** that the rule ends the bargaining **while contending** that it also ends the record"), and no distractor in the set carries one. `check-grant-frame.mjs` (new) flags an option only on a grant verb PLUS a limiting pivot — a bare "accepts the offer" is not a concession — and splits credit across carriers so that a set where all four options are framed scores 0.25 wherever the key sits; the self-test fails if the four key positions do not sum to exactly 1.0000. In the held batch it reaches 3 items of 24, so it cannot be the mechanism behind that batch's +47.2 attack margin, and `sat-ii-hard-v1` — the worst blind margin this register holds at 93.0% — has **zero** framed sets, which confirms from the other direction that its stance tell is semantic and no string test will ever see it. | | as published | corrected |
|---|---|---|
| live bank, all domains | 955 sets, 31.3%, **+6.3** | **273 sets of 989, 47.9%, +22.9** |
| Advanced Math | 33.1%, +8.1 | 91 sets, 46.2%, **+21.2** |

| `sat-adv-hard-v1` (held) | +23.9 | 14 sets, **+37.5** |

So "a mild elevation, not a rewrite programme" was an artefact of averaging in 682 sets that could not score anything but control. - **2026-09-04** — **THE MATH SANDBOX COULD NOT SEE A SIGN ERROR, AND MATH HAS NO OTHER GATE.** An authoring agent mutation-tested three of its own keys and, in passing, noted that `normHash` strips signs so `"-20"` and `"20"` hash alike — its item survived only because `asNumber` caught it first. Chased, and the hole is real and wider than the note: `answersMatch` compares numerically ONLY when both sides parse as a plain number or simple fraction; everything else fell through to `normHash`, which removes every non-alphanumeric character including the minus. Proved against six cases before touching anything — **four FALSE PASSES**: `-20i` vs `20i`, `-2x + 5` vs `2x + 5`, `x = -4` vs `x = 4`, and `-1/(x^2+3x)` vs `1/(x^2+3x)`, **which is the exact option shape of the Advanced Math batch.** This is not an ordinary bug: R&W has a blind attack and a human sitting behind it, but for math the sandbox IS the gate, so a comparison blind to sign is a gate that cannot fail on a whole class of mis-key. Fixed with a separate `normAnswer` that preserves `+ - / ^ .`; `normHash` is deliberately untouched because it also produces `content_hash` and changing it would rewrite every dedup hash in the bank. All four sign cases now caught, four genuine-match cases (prose key, expression key, whitespace, fraction) still match, and every existing math batch re-verifies unchanged: alg-hard-v1 24/24, adv-hard-v2 24/24, psda-hard-v1 32/32, act-math-v2c 30/30, act-math-v3nq 24/24. **The lesson is about where the finding came from.** It was not found by a checker, a test, or a review — it came from an author volunteering an aside about why its own mutation test passed. The mutation test was in the brief; the aside was not. Asking authors to break their own gate and then to say WHY it held is worth more than asking them to report that it held. → **B6**

- **2026-09-04** — 65 MATH ITEMS BANKED, AND AN EIGHTH STRUCTURAL PROXY THAT IS REAL, BANK-WIDE, AND SURVIVES THE DRAW SHUFFLE. Three batches (ACT Number and Quantity, ACT Statistics and Probability, SAT PSDA) graded together: **all 72 keys re-derived by an independent method and all 72 correct, no `single_defensible: false` anywhere** — the first clean sweep of that size. Difficulty came back 17% / 17% / 12.5% hard against self-labels of 8 / 8 / 10, and the grader named the reason precisely: the demotions are almost all one shape, where the second constraint is real but **the stem announces it** ("sold only in bottles… least number that must be bought", "selected from among those who did NOT pass", a capitalised "EXACTLY ONE"). That is a well-built medium, not a hard. **THE NEW TELL: THE KEY IS RARELY THE EXTREME VALUE.** Found by reading three batches as a set — the key was the largest option in 7 of 62 numeric items (11% against 25%), and 1 of 18 in PSDA, so "eliminate the largest" was a free elimination. `check-key-magnitude.mjs` (new, self-tested including a flat-control fixture) measures the rank of the key's VALUE, and because this is decidable it was run over the whole population rather than sampled:

| | rank 1 (smallest) | 2 | 3 | 4 (largest) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| live bank, 1,432 numeric items | 17% | 33% | 32% | **18%** |
| the three candidate batches, 64 | 16% | 38% | 36% | **11%** |

So the batches were modestly worse than a baseline that is **itself skewed** — the whole bank avoids both extremes, and eliminating them takes a solver from 25% to about 33%. **It is not fixed by shuffling**, which is what separates it from the positional cycle and the ABCD permutation recorded earlier today: those are about letters and die at `shuffleDrawnChoices`, while this is about VALUES and a student can eliminate the largest number wherever it sits. The cause is the authoring brief, not chance: the "forgot the last step / didn't convert the unit" distractor is systematically LARGER than the key (8640 seconds, 108 dollars, 28 km, 20000 members). The fix is to vary which direction the incomplete answer points — reshuffling would also break the ascending-order convention both real exams use. **Banked at the grader's difficulty after its drops**: SP15 (redundant with SP01 and SP06, and its answer needs a bar read halfway between gridlines), plus one member of each matched pair where solving one hands over the other — SP05/SP16, H2-05/H2-24, and H2-23/NQ09, which are **the same pump item in two different batches**. 23 + 22 + 20 inserted; ACT Math 160 -> 197 with Number and Quantity 16 -> 35 and Statistics 18 -> 36, PSDA hard 45 -> 48. **Two items carry no machine gate and are marked hand-checked**: H2-04 and H2-22 are prose "which conclusion is appropriate" items whose `solve` snippets are string templates restating the intended answer rather than deriving it. They are also the same form with the same key letter, which the grader flagged as a pair a student could learn. **A renderer constraint worth keeping**: `QuestionGraphicView` draws no value labels on bar/scatter/line, only five ticks at max/4 — so any item whose answer needs a value between gridlines is unreadable in the app, which is very likely part of why 80.6% of maths figures once scored decorative. Every surviving figure item here has its answer on a tick. → **A21**, **B6**

- **2026-09-04** — **SECOND CORRECTION TO THE SAME NUMBER, AND THE DEFECT IS A TENTH OF WHAT I SAID TWICE.** The symbolic-hub population figure has now been published wrong twice, both times confidently:

| | structured sets | key-is-hub | margin | why it was wrong |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| first published | 955 of 989 | 31.3% | +6.3 | every all-numeric set scored **exactly** the 25% control, diluting the real signal |
| "CORRECTION" | 273 of 989 | 47.9% | **+22.9** | the guard counted TOKENS, and `-6` is two tokens and `1/2` is three — so any numeric set containing a negative or a fraction still leaked in |
| **now** | **38 of 1009** | **28.3%** | **+3.3** | guard asks "is every option a NUMBER?", which is the question that was always meant |

**Caught by an authoring agent, not by me, and it had already cost them work**: the Algebra v2 author reported that a first draft scored 16.7pts and they had rewritten three option sets to clear it — then noticed the guard "does not fire when any option carries a minus sign or is written as `a/b`" and said so. Three sound option sets were rewritten to satisfy a broken number.

**The corrected detector is verified against known data before being believed**, which is the only reason to trust the third figure: `sat-adv-hard-v1` — the batch three solvers cracked at 51.4% on the options-only attack — now reads **90.5% over its 7 genuinely symbolic sets**, against 62.5% under the old guard. Sharper on the case whose answer is known, which is what a better detector does. Self-tests added for the three shapes that escaped: bare numbers with a negative, bare numbers with a fraction, and a sign-closed quad.

**What this actually means for the bank.** The symbolic hub is NOT a bank-wide defect and never was. It is 38 sets of 1,009 at +3.3 — and it was catastrophic in exactly one authoring cohort (v1, +65.5) and near-absent everywhere else. **That is the same shape as the 2026-08-06 arithmetic-hub finding**, where "bank-wide 64.4%" turned out to be 98.3% in one repaired cohort and 8.0% in the other 730 items. Twice now, a defect measured across a population has turned out to live almost entirely in one batch, and both times the first instinct was a rewrite programme. **A THIRD CHECKER CAUGHT LYING THE SAME DAY.** `check-absolute-tell.mjs` ignores `argv` entirely and queries five hardcoded bank pairs; four authoring agents were told to run it on a batch file and it printed the LIVE BANK's numbers as though they described their file. The SSAT Verbal author noticed and said so instead of pasting the number — "it never opened my file. This is exactly the trap in CLAUDE.md." It now exits 2 on any file argument. That is three checkers in one day that reported a plausible number about a file they had not read: `check-math-hub` over an empty population, `check-symbolic-hub` over sets it could not see, and this one over the wrong data entirely. → **B6**

- **2026-09-04** — **NO CHECKER IN THIS REPO COULD READ A FIVE-CHOICE ITEM, AND A LIVE SSAT COHORT WENT IN UNMEASURED BECAUSE OF IT.** Found by an SSAT Math author who read the DENOMINATOR rather than the colour: `check-math-hub.mjs` printed "0 of 40 option sets have a derivational structure this checker can read (40 unscorable)" — which is zero coverage, not a pass. Three separate four-choice assumptions were stacked in one function: a `length !== 4` guard, a distinctness test comparing against the literal `4` rather than the set size, and a hardcoded 25% control in the reporter. Widening only the first left the count at zero, which is why the second and third were found at all. `check-key-magnitude.mjs` had the same shape — it hardcoded ranks 1-4 and a 25% control, so on SSAT it **silently dropped rank 5** and its printed percentages summed to 83%. The author noticed the columns did not add up. **The fixed checker replicates their independent generalisation exactly**: `ssat-math-s7` (new) 0.0% against a 20% control, margin -20.0; **`ssat-math-s6`, which is LIVE, 36.1% against 20%, margin +16.1 over 18 structured sets, with the same eight hub items they named** (SM6-01, -08, -22, -24, -31, -39, -41, -42). Same numbers, same items, two independent routes — which is the only reason to trust a detector that has been wrong three times today. **So a 45-item cohort shipped over the 10-point bar and nobody could see it**, because the instrument silently declined to look. That is the fourth checker caught today reporting something other than what it measured, after `check-math-hub` over an empty population, `check-symbolic-hub` over sets it could not see, and `check-absolute-tell` over the wrong data entirely. The pattern in all four is identical and worth stating once: **a checker that cannot process its input must say so loudly; every one of these printed a number instead.** SSAT and ISEE items are five-choice and four-choice respectively, and every proxy in this directory was written against SAT's four. Assume any checker is four-choice until its self-test proves otherwise. → **B6**

## 6. The rule that keeps this honest

A cohort is **not** clean because the cheap checks passed. Five
structural proxies have been built — letter spread, length rank,
punctuation asymmetry, concessive pivot, option-family balance — and
each caught the tell it was built for while missing the next one. Two
more were added on 2026-09-04 and behaved the same way: the symbolic
derivational hub (real, +6.3 bank-wide, arithmetic and therefore worth
running) and the option grant-frame (real, and present on 2% of the
bank). Seven for seven. The
blind attack is the gate, a human sitting is the confirmation, and the
structural checks are pre-flight only. See CLAUDE.md.

- **2026-09-04** — I COMMISSIONED A BATCH THIS DIRECTORY ALREADY RECORDS AS DEAD. Two authors were briefed for SSAT and ISEE reading under the authored-key design, ~280k tokens spent, while `READING-PILOT-KILLED.md:138` already read "Do not attempt a reading v3 under the authored-key design." I wrote both briefs off this register's open-work rows, which said "SSAT/ISEE reading thin — **but see READING-PILOT-KILLED.md before commissioning: the authored-key design is 4-for-4 dead**" and did not link the kill. Both files are in `quarantine/`; neither is to be graded or inserted. The salvage is a FOURTH relocation of the same tell — qualifier -> moderation -> tension -> **altitude**: the SSAT author's keys were the second-order option (about the inquiry, the evidence, the observer) against four first-order distractors, nameable with no passage and worth 10 of 36 cold. Every earlier fix moved the tell sideways in phrasing; this one moved it up a level, which is why v2's whole remediation list was clean while the batch stayed solvable. **Before commissioning any batch, grep this directory for a KILLED file naming that section** — the register's open-work row is not sufficient, and is what failed here. _(quarantined; both reading rows now link the kill file)_

- **2026-09-04** — EIGHTH STRUCTURAL PROXY BUILT, AND IT REPRODUCED THE MATH-HUB LESSON RATHER THAN FINDING A NEW PROBLEM. A PSDA author's own ad-hoc scan caught what `check-math-hub`, `check-key-magnitude` and the sandbox all missed: the key was the exact PRODUCT of two distractors (`P(both) = P(first) x P(second|first)`, both factors sitting in the option set). Different relation from the hub — the hub asks "is the key one edit from everything else", this asks "is the key the arithmetic composition of two others" — so a set can be hub-clean and composition-dirty, which is how it got through. `check-composition.mjs` now measures it over the WHOLE live bank, because the defect is arithmetic and therefore decidable; no sampling. **The result is that the defect is one cohort, not the bank:**

      four-choice, sat/math/v2 alone   148 fires   51 key   +9.5   z=2.66
      four-choice, EVERYTHING ELSE     124 fires   31 key    0.0   z=0.00
      five-choice (SSAT), pooled        51 fires   16 key  +11.4   z=2.03

  Everything outside that one authoring cohort sits at *exactly* chance. The excess is about 14 items in sat/math/v2 and about 6 across SSAT — roughly **20 items bank-wide**, a surgical repair, not a programme. The two headline cohorts in the per-cohort table (`ssat-math-v1` at +55.0, `ssat-math-s4` at +30.0) are **3 of 4 fires and 2 of 4 fires** and are noise; quoting either as a finding would be the small-cohort error the answer-key-spread guard already recorded.

  Two of my own errors, both caught by the checks rather than by reading the output: (1) two of the three self-test fixtures I wrote were wrong — one had duplicate options and one contained TWO compositions, so the strategy correctly declined to fire and the self-test failed. I fixed the fixtures, not the checker. (2) I selected `choices` and `correct_answer` as columns on `study_item_bank`; they live inside the `item` JSONB and PostgREST rejected the query outright. That is the good failure — the same guess against a column that happened to exist is how this project has produced wrong numbers before, and it is why the shape is now taken from `check-math-hub` rather than from memory. _(checker committed with selftest; the ~20 excess items are open work)_

- **2026-09-04** — A CHECKER REPORTED "4 measure(s) failed" OVER DATA IT HAD NEVER READ, and two authors hit it independently within an hour. `check-batch-variety.mjs` reads `stimulus ?? passage`. SSAT and ISEE Verbal items carry neither (`passage` is null on all 180 live SSAT Verbal rows), so `filter(Boolean)` emptied the array and every threshold compared against `NaN` — which fails every comparison. It printed four confident FAILs, and printed **the identical output for the batch under test and for a matched sample of the live shipped bank**, because neither was measured. That is the same shape as the verifier that reported "0 problems" over a bank PostgREST had truncated at 1000 rows. It now exits 2 with an explanation, as `check-absolute-tell.mjs` already does. Verified both ways: refuses a no-stimulus file, still measures a real passage batch. _(fixed on the spot)_

- **2026-09-04** — A STAGED BATCH WAS EDITED BY AN UNIDENTIFIED PROCESS. `isee-verbal-s7.batch.json` showed 40 of 40 items with reordered options, **7 with different option sets and 2 with different keys** (IV7-24 vague->evasive, IV7-27 discrepancy->gap). No agent claimed the change; two separate authors independently reported that their scratchpad scripts had been overwritten mid-task by a concurrent agent, one of which ran and printed another cohort's output under its own command. The content changes look like plausible distractor improvements rather than corruption — which is precisely why they are dangerous: nobody reviewed them, and two of them move a KEY. Working copy preserved at `quarantine/isee-verbal-s7.UNATTRIBUTED.json`, file restored to HEAD. **Concurrent agents must not share a scratchpad directory, and no batch should be inserted from a working tree whose diff nobody can attribute.** _(restored; the shared-scratchpad collision is open)_

- **2026-09-04** — TWO BATCHES FAILED THEIR GATE TODAY AND NEITHER GETS A REWRITE. The standing rule is one failed distractor rewrite then stop, because a rewrite has twice inverted a tell rather than removing it.

  **TOEFL Daily Life v6** — 24 items, six fresh solvers, split so no solver sees two items from one passage, keys dealt 3/3/3/3. **56.9% against a 25.0% control, +31.9; bar is under 35%.** Caveat that weakens it: only 3 distinct pick-strings across 6 solvers, and the pre-registered rule calls identical pick-strings "no verdict". The per-item split is the real finding and it is perfectly clean: every item whose key **contradicts** the institutional default went 0/3 (tags by phone not website, price by coat not size, one shared pen); every item whose key **is** the default went 3/3 (out-of-hours referral, physical card not a photo, no spare parts in the van). Four of the five hard items were solved blind — hard WITH the passage, free without it. **The brief is the defect, not the authoring:** dl-fresh requires ONE atypical fact per passage and one question testing it, which leaves the second question of each pair free to test a default-conforming fact, and that is where all the leakage sits. A v7 needs both questions turning on a non-default fact, with atypicality verified against a check rather than the author's intuition — this author believed a 14-day pre-arrival vaccination rule was atypical and it is the kennel norm.

  **SAT Information and Ideas hard v2** — 24 items, three no-source rounds, two solvers each. 21/18 -> 19/18 -> **16/18 of 24 against a chance of 6**, i.e. 67-75% against a bar of ≤33%. Worth recording HOW it moved: round 1 failed on an unnamed rule (the key reconciles or bounds the tension while distractors collapse it four visible ways). Rebuilding every option set introduced a **new** tell — a direction-reversed mirror twin in nearly every set, cutting 4 options to 2 before reading. That is the tell-inversion pattern again, inside a single session. Residual exploits the solvers named: quantitative keys pair both quantities or convert counts to rates (solves 4 items outright), and real-world knowledge settles 4 more with no structure at all.

  Both authors correctly flagged the calibration caveat rather than hiding behind it: model blind attacks over-report, and this repo has the numbers — the ACT cohorts scored 76-79% by model and **10%** by the human co-founder. So neither number is a verdict on its own. Both batches take the ACT disposition: **held, not archived, and a human sitting decides.** Do not commission a v3 of either. _(held; joins the human-sitting queue behind B7)_
